question: According to the passage, which is the main pigment in algae for photosynthesis?
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage describes algae as **photosynthetic creatures** that rely on specific pigments to capture light energy.
 
• It explicitly identifies **chlorophyll** as the "principal pigment" that allows these organisms to perform photosynthesis.
 
• The text states that even though algae are a diverse (multiphyletic) group, having **chlorophyll** is the "one thing in common" among them.
 
• None of the other pigments listed (Melanin, Xanthophyll, or Carotenoid) are mentioned in the passage as the primary pigment for algae.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence from Text:** *"They [algae] are eukaryotes with the **principal pigment being chlorophyll**, which allows them to perform photosynthesis."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: Melanin** – This is a pigment found in humans and animals responsible for skin and hair color; it is not involved in photosynthesis.
 
• **Option 3 & 4: Xanthophyll and Carotenoid** – While these are indeed accessory pigments found in many types of algae in real-world biology, they are **not mentioned** in the provided text, which identifies chlorophyll as the primary one.
